description: The plot illustrates the accuracy of different models as a function of the number of demonstrations on the 'BBQ' task. The x-axis is labeled '#Demonstrations', has a linear scale, ranges from 0 to 1500, and has tick labels at intervals of 250. The y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy', has a linear scale, ranges from 45 to 55, and has tick labels at intervals of 5. The 'Squared Exponential' model, represented by a dark blue solid line with circle markers, starts at an accuracy of approximately 52 at 0 demonstrations and increases steadily to around 56.5 at 250 demonstrations, before stabilizing at this value until 1500 demonstrations. The 'Tanh' model, shown as a blue solid line with circle markers, begins at about 48 accuracy at 0 demonstrations and shows a slight decline to around 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'ELU' model, depicted as a light blue solid line with circle markers, starts at 46 accuracy and shows a gradual increase to around 47.5 at 1000 demonstrations, remaining steady until 1500 demonstrations. The 'LLaMA-2-chat-7B' model is represented by a pink dashed line and maintains a consistent accuracy of around 43 across all demonstration points.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy of different models as a function of the number of demonstrations, providing a comparison of performance trends on the 'BBQ' task. The x-axis is labeled '#Demonstrations', with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1500 and tick labels at intervals of 250 demonstrations. The y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy', with a linear scale ranging from 45 to 55, and tick labels at intervals of 5. The 'Squared Exponential' model starts at an accuracy of approximately 52 at 0 demonstrations, increases steadily to 56 at 250 demonstrations, and then stabilizes. The 'Tanh' model begins at about 48 accuracy at 0 demonstrations and shows a slight decline to 47 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'ELU' model starts at 46 accuracy and shows a gradual increase to 48 at 1500 demonstrations. The 'LLmA-2-chat-7B' model maintains a consistent accuracy of 43 across all demonstration points, performing significantly worse than the other models. The 'Squared Exponential' model consistently outperforms all other models, with the 'ELU' model showing the second-best performance overall.
